FREQUENT USE OF CHEMICAL FERTILIZERS AND PESTICIDES

2614. SHRI TAMILSELVAN THANGA:

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state:

(a) whether it is a fact that the frequent use of Chemical Fertilizers and Pesticides on Environment to yield more agriculture produce results in very hazardous effect on human health and destroy human life also;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether the Union Government has ever assessed the effect of frequent use of Chemical Fertilizers and Pesticides on Environment and human health;

(d) if so, the details thereof;

(e) whether the Union Government has find out the alternative ways to rationalize the frequent use of Chemical Fertilizers and Pesticides on Environment; and

(f) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND

FARMERS WELFARE (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR):

(a) to (d) Chemical fertilizers used judiciously as per recommended doses are not harmful. Government promotes judicious use of fertilizer through Soil Health and Fertility scheme. The scheme provides Soil Health Cards (SHCs) for farm holdings, to promote balanced and integrated nutrient management for improving productivity and soil fertility. Soil samples are processed as per standard procedures and analyzed for parameters such as pH, Electrical16.12.2025 439 Conductivity, Organic Carbon, available Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Sulphur, and micronutrients (Zinc, Copper, Iron, Manganese and Boron). The diagnostic soil health assessment of farmer fields is taken up periodically so as to issue SHCs at least once in 3 years. Since 2014-15, 25.61 crore Soil Health Cards have been generated till date. Under the scheme, Rs. 1970 Crore has been released since inception. 93, 781 farmers' trainings, 6.80 lakh demonstrations, 7425 farmer's melas/ campaigns on SHC have been organized across the country.

The Registration Committee, constituted under Section 5 of the Insecticides Act, 1968 registers pesticides after considering its efficacy and safety to human beings, animals and environment. Pesticides used as per the approved label claims and leaflets are unlikely to cause any harm. In addition, technical reviews are carried out from time to time to assess the safety of pesticides for their continued use.

(e) and (f) The Government of India has notified Organic fertilizers, Bio-fertilizers, De-oiled cake, Organic Carbon Enhancer and Nano fertilizer in The Fertilizer Control Order, 1985 to ensure quality sale of these fertilizers. Government is promoting Natural Farming and Organic Farming as alternatives to chemical farming for sustainable agriculture and human wellbeing. Organic farming in the country is implemented through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) in all the States/UTs other-than North Eastern States, and Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) exclusively for North Eastern region. Farmers are provided assistance from production to16.12.2025 440 marketing under the organic farming schemes. Further, the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) was approved by the Union Cabinet on 25.11.2024 to promote Natural Farming across the country. The Mission has been initiated to strengthen agriculture practices with scientifically backed agro ecological approaches towards sustainability, climate resilience and safe food.

NATIONAL SURVEY CONDUCTED UNDER NAMASTE SCHEME

2615. SHRI BALRAM NAIK PORIKA:

Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:

(a) the total number of manual scavengers identified in the country through the National Survey conducted under the NAMASTE scheme till November 2025, State-wise;

(b) the number of deaths of sewer/septic tank workers reported during cleaning operations since 2019 along with the compensation paid;

(c) the concrete steps taken to enforce the complete ban on manual entry into sewers/septic tanks and to ensure hundred per cent mechanisation of cleaning operations;

(d) the number of identified manual scavengers who have been provided rehabilitation assistance, skill training and self-employment loans under the NAMASTE scheme; and

(e) whether the Government proposes to bring further amendments to the Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013, for stricter penalties and16.12.2025 441 time-bound eradication and if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND

EMPOWERMENT (SHRI RAMDAS ATHAWALE):

(a) A Nationwide survey, covering 4800+ Urban Local Bodies, has been conducted for identification of Sewer and Septic Tank workers (SSWs) under NAMASTE scheme and not for identification of Manual Scavengers.

(b) According to the information provided by the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK), 471 sanitation workers have lost their lives due to hazardous cleaning of sewer and septic tanks since 2019 (upto 31.10.2025) and full and partial compensation has been paid to the families of 397 and 19 deceased, respectively.

(c) Section 7 of the "Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013" prohibits hazardous cleaning of a Sewer or a Septic Tank.

To tackle hazardous cleaning of Sewer and Septic Tanks, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment in convergence with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs launched the "National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE)" Scheme in 2023-24 for implementation in all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) of the country. The objective is to ensure safety and dignity of Sewer and Septic Tank Workers (SSWs) and to empower them socially and economically. The aim is also to achieve zero fatality in sanitation work and to ensure that no sanitation worker comes in direct contact with human faecal matter.

16.12.2025 442

Steps taken under NAMASTE scheme to avoid manual entry into sewer and septic tanks and to ensure mechanised cleaning of sewer and septic tanks are as under:-

i. Safety devices to Emergency Response Sanitation Units (ERSUs).

ii. Upfront Capital Subsidy to sanitation workers and Private Sanitation Service Operators (PSSOs) for procurement of sanitation related machine/equipment.

iii. Occupational Safety training to the sewer and septic tank workers.

iv. Workshops on prevention of hazardous cleaning of sewer and septic tanks.

Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) launched Swachh Bharat Mission – Urban (SBM-U) 2.0 on 1st, October, 2021. It includes a new component i.e. Used Water management (UWM) with one of the objectives of eradication of hazardous entry into sewers and septic tanks and elimination of manual cleaning, through mechanization of sewer and septic tank cleaning operations.

Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has also issued the following advisory for safe cleaning of sewer and septic tanks:-

i. Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for cleaning of Sewer or Septic tank.

ii. Advisory for technical and managerial interventions for ensuring safety during sewer and septic tank cleaning through Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU).

iii. Ready Reckoner for Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) for ensuring safety of16.12.2025 443 sanitation workers.

iv. Organising Safaimitra Suraksha Shivirs nationwide through ULBs to provide health check-ups and linkages to social welfare schemes.

v. Issued protocol for Safai Mitra Surakshit Shehar.

(d) Components of the erstwhile 'Self-Employment Scheme for the Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (SRMS)' have been subsumed in the NAMASTE scheme in 2023-24 and rehabilitation assistance provided to manual scavengers and their dependents under it is given below:-

SI. No. Components Number of Beneficiaries
1 Onetime Cash Assistance 58098 (Full saturation)
2 Skill Development Training 27928
3 Capital Subsidy for self-employment project 2652

(e) There is no proposal at present to amend the "Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013 (MS Act, 2013)".

FDI FOR DATA CENTRE PROJECTS

2616. SHRI PRAVEEN PATEL:

SHRIMATI MAHIMA KUMARI MEWAR:

CAPTAIN BRIJESH CHOWTA:

SHRI DARSHAN SINGH CHOUDHARY:

SHRI VISHNU DAYAL RAM:

SHRI YADUVEER WADIYAR:

SHRI PUTTA MAHESH KUMAR:

SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB:

SHRI ANIL FIROJIYA:

16.12.2025 444

SHRI RAVINDRA SHUKLA ALIAS RAVI KISHAN:

Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:

(a) the total Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) committed for data centre projects in India uptill financial year 2029-30;

(b) the total FDI contribution by major hyperscalers and domestic operators;

(c) whether any proposals of the Government specifically include Dakshina Kannada districts in Karnataka given its proximity to a major port and availability of reliable power infrastructure, if so, the timeline for its approval, commencement and expected operationalisation of such proposals;

(d) whether the Government has identified key policy bottlenecks affecting FDI inflow into the data centre sector, if so, the measures being taken by the Government to streamline tax-related clearances, environmental approvals and other sector specific permissions;

(e) the details regarding the list of major companies who have invested in India to establish data centres in the country during the last five years especially in Andhra Pradesh; and

(f) the total FDI contribution by such companies and that of domestic operators?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND

INDUSTRY; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF

ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI JITIN

PRASADA):

(a) and (b) No such data is maintained by DPIIT. FDI inflows depend on a host16.12.2025 445 of factors such as availability of natural resources, market size, infrastructure, political and general investment climate as well as macroeconomic stability and investment decisions of foreign investors.

(c) Karnataka Data Centre (DC) Policy 2022-2027 promotes Data Centre companies to setup Data Centres in the beyond Bengaluru region, which includes Dakshina Kannada districts of geographies like Mangaluru and Mysuru.

(d) To promote Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), including FDI inflow in data centre, the Government has put in place an investor friendly policy.

Government of India vide Gazette notification number F. No. 13/1/2017- INF dated 11th October 2022 has included data centres in the Harmonization Master List of Infrastructure sub-sectors. Further, to ensure that India remains an attractive and investor friendly destination, the Government reviews the FDI policy on a continuous basis and makes changes from time to time after holding extensive consultations with stakeholders including apex industry chambers, associations, representatives of industries/groups and other organizations, considering their views/comments.

(e) and (f) No such state-wise data for data centre is centrally maintained.

WILDLIFE SMUGGLING THROUGH NORTHEAST BORDERS

2617. DR. AMAR SINGH:

Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:

16.12.2025 446

(a) whether the Ministry is aware of increased wildlife smuggling through India's northeast borders involving exotic species from South-East Asia and Latin America;

(b) if so, the number of wildlife smuggling cases registered in the northeast States in the past five years, State-wise breakup and the conviction rate in such cases;

(c) whether the Border Security Force, Assam Rifles and other paramilitary forces deployed in the northeast have been trained and equipped to detect and prevent wildlife trafficking; and

(d) if so, the details of such training programmes and coordination mechanisms with wildlife protection agencies?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI

NITYANAND RAI):

(a) and (b) The Ministry is aware of wildlife smuggling at the borders, however, the Border Guarding Forces are effectively countering this issue by apprehending criminals. There have been cases of wildlife smuggling and its seizures in the States of Assam, Manipur, Mizoram, Meghalaya and Tripura. The details of number of cases registered and conviction rates in such cases, state- wise, are not maintained by the Ministry.

(c) and (d) The Border Guarding Forces (BGFs) do not possess any specialized training or equipment dedicated to detecting wildlife trafficking. The wildlife trafficking cases are detected whenever their smuggling takes place across the border during regular border surveillance. If any wildlife / exotic16.12.2025 447 species are recovered/seized during border surveillance, the same are handed over to the Forest Departments/Customs Departments of the concerned States.

There are mechanisms in place for coordination with the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB). District-level meetings with the concerned civil authorities are being held regularly in which such types of issues are discussed and coordinated.

FISHERIES AND ANIMAL HUSBANDRY SCHEMES IN KARNATAKA

2618. SHRI M. MALLESH BABU:

Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to state:

(a) the details of Central assistance funds released to the State of Karnataka under the Blue Revolution Scheme, the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) and earlier fisheries development schemes since 2004-05, year-wise;

(b) the total number of beneficiaries, cooperatives and self-help groups supported for inland, marine and brackish-water fisheries development in Karnataka under Central schemes;

(c) the number and location of veterinary hospitals, dispensaries, mobile veterinary units, artificial insemination centres and breeding farms established or upgraded in Karnataka;

(d) the total fish production, export value and contribution of Karnataka to country's overall fisheries sector since 2004-05; and16.12.2025 448 (e) the details of infrastructure created under PMMSY and other related schemes in coastal districts Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Uttara Kannada and Karwar, including fishing harbours, fish landing centres, cold chain facilities and processing units?

THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ; AND MINISTER OF FISHERIES,

ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING (SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS

LALAN SINGH):

(a) The details of central assistance funds released to the Government of Karnataka under the Blue Revolution Scheme, the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) and earlier fisheries development schemes since 2004-05, year-wise are given in the enclosed Statement-I.

(b) Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) implemented by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India, the end level beneficiaries are identified by the respective State Governments. The State Government of Karnataka has informed that a total of 4538 beneficiaries including Cooperatives and Self-Help Groups have been benefitted under inland, marine and brackish- water fisheries development in Karnataka under the PMMSY during 2020-2025.

(c) The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), GoI has informed that under the 'Establishment and Strengthening of Veterinary Hospitals and Dispensaries-Mobile Veterinary Units' (ESVHD-MVU) of Livestock Health and Disease Control Program (LHDCP) financial support is provided to the States/UTs including Karnataka for operation of Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) to provide diagnosis, treatment at farmer's doorstep. It is informed that at present, 697 Veterinary Hospitals/Polyclinics, 2,176 Veterinary Dispensaries,16.12.2025 449 and 275 Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) are functioning in the State. Besides, as per information received from the State Government, currently there are 7119 Artificial insemination centres and 21 Breeding farms in Karnataka.

(d) Karnataka is one of the potential state in terms of fisheries sector and contributes significantly to the country's fisheries sector. Government of Karnataka has reported that fish production of Government of Karnataka has increased from 2.51 lakh tonnes in 2004-2005 to 9.63 lakh tonnes during 2024- 25. In addition, the export value of fish and fisheries products from Karnataka has increased from Rs.76.92 Crore in 2004-05 to Rs.4048 crore in 2023-24.

Currently Karnataka contributes to about 5% to country's fish production and about 7% to country's export value.

(e) Under the PMMSY and other related schemes of GoI, projects are approved based on the proposals submitted by the respective State Government. As reported by Government of Karnataka, the details of infrastructure created under PMMSY and other related schemes in coastal districts of Karnataka is given in the enclosed Statement-II.

CROP LOSSES DUE TO CLIMATE EXTREMES

2620. SHRI DEEPENDER SINGH HOODA:

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS' WELFARE be pleased to state:

(a) the total crop loss during the last ten years including the current year, along with the valuation of such losses, year, State and Union Territory-wise;

(b) the total compensation provided to farmers for such crop losses during the last ten years including the current year, year-wise, State-wise and Union Territory-wise;

(c) the steps taken by the Government to prevent crop failures arising out of climate change and irrigation deficits; and16.12.2025 452 (d) whether the Government has prepared a roadmap with a definite timeline to effectively control and minimise such losses in the future?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND

FARMERS WELFARE (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR):

(a) and (b) Information on crop loss is not maintained centrally. As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the primary responsibility for disaster management, including disbursal of relief assistance to the affected, rests with the State Government concerned. State Governments undertake relief measures in the wake of natural calamities, from the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) already placed at their disposal as per approved norms. Additional financial assistance is provided from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), in case of disaster of 'severe nature'. Details of the fund allocated and released under SDRF/NDRF to the States are available on website i.e. ndmindia.mha.gov.in.

To provide relief to farmers suffering crop losses, Government also launched Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY) in the country from Kharif 2016 season implemented on 'Area Approach' basis. The Scheme provides comprehensive risk coverage against crop damage from pre-sowing to post- harvest for cereals, millets and pulses or oilseeds, and commercial or horticultural crops notified by concerned State Government. The scheme safeguards against widespread yield loss due to natural risks, such as, flood, inundation, landslide, drought, dry spells, hailstorm, cyclone, pests/diseases, natural fire/lightning, storm, typhoon, tempest, hurricane, and tornado, localized16.12.2025 453 risks (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst, and natural fire) and post- harvest losses due to cyclone, unseasonal rain, and hailstorm. As of 30.11.2025, ₹1,90,374 crore has been disbursed as claims to approximately 2,301 lakh farmers since inception of the Scheme. Detail of coverage and claims paid to the insured farmers since inception i.e. 2016-17 to 2024-25 is given in the enclosed Statement.

(c) and (d) The Government implements National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) to deal with the adverse climate situations in the agriculture sector. Under NMSA, Per Drop More Crop(PDMC) scheme is being implemented to increase water use efficiency at the farm level through micro irrigation technologies i.e. drip and sprinkler irrigation systems. Rainfed Area Development scheme is focuses on Integrated Farming System for enhancing productivity and minimizing risks associated with climatic variability. The Soil Health and Fertility scheme assists states in promoting Integrated Nutrient Management through judicious use of chemical fertilizers including secondary and micronutrients in conjunction with organic manures and bio-fertilizers.

Organic farming is promoted through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana and Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region and natural farming through National Mission on Natural Farming. Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture, Agroforestry and National Bamboo Mission also promote climate resilience in agriculture.

Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has been implementing a project- National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) since16.12.2025 454 2011. The project studies the impact of erratic monsoons, extreme weather events and climate change on agriculture. District level risk and vulnerability assessment of agriculture to future climate change and integrated simulation modelling studies for estimating the future projections of climate change are undertaken. Risk and vulnerability assessment of agriculture to climate change has been carried out for 651 predominantly agricultural districts as per Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) protocols. 310 districts were identified as vulnerable out of which 109 districts have been categorized as 'very high' and 201 districts as 'highly' vulnerable. To address the impact of climate change, ICAR has released 2900 varieties during last 10 years (2014- 2024). Out of these 2661 varieties are tolerant to one or more biotic and/or abiotic stresses.

SC AND OBC POST-MATRIC SCHOLARSHIPS

2621. SHRI M. K. RAGHAVAN:

Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:

(a) whether the Government has taken steps to resolve delays and backlogs in the payment of SC and OBC post-matric scholarships in the States and if so, the details thereof;

(b) whether the Government is considering any revision to scholarship rates in view of rising academic expenses and if so, the details thereof along with the timeframe set in this regard; and16.12.2025 456 (c) whether the Government has received any representations from States regarding technical glitches in scholarship portals affecting timely approvals and if so, the details thereof along with the action taken thereon?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND

EMPOWERMENT (SHRI RAMDAS ATHAWALE):

(a) The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE) implements Centrally sponsored Post Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC students through State Government/UT Administrations on Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode w.e.f 2021-22. Central share is released directly into the Aadhaar seeded bank account of the beneficiaries. The release of central share is contingent upon States/UTs transmitting their State/UT share paid data to the Central portal/National Scholarship Portal (NSP). The aforementioned scheme is open- ended and demand driven for the eligible students of all the recognised institutions across India.

Ministry is also implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post Matric scholarship for the students belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Backward Classes (EBC), and De-Notified Tribes (DNTs).

Steps taken by the Government for effective implementation of the aforementioned schemes are as under:

• Periodic review by holding meetings at National level, Regional level, State level and field visits by Senior Officers.

• On-boarding of Schemes on National Scholarship Portal and online end to end processing.

16.12.2025 457

• Regular hand holding meetings/workshops for National Scholarship Portal (NSP) on-boarded States/UTs having their own scholarship portals.

(b) For Post Matric scholarship scheme for SCs and Post Matric scholarship for OBCs, EBCs and DNTs, as per approval of Expenditure Finance Committee and the Cabinet, current scholarship rate is effective till FY 2025-26. Review and revision of the Schemes which also covers the scholarship rates follow a laid down procedure.

(c) For effective and transparent implementation of the Schemes, Scholarships are released through the designated portal. Further, the technical glitches reported are addressed and resolved promptly through the portal.

CANDIDATES TRAINED UNDER PM DAKSH YOJANA

2622. SHRI PUSHPENDRA SAROJ:

Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:

(a) the number of candidates trained under the PM-DAKSH Yojana since 2021, year-wise by social category and State-wise, particularly district-wise for Uttar Pradesh;

(b) the number of beneficiaries trained under each component and those placed or selfemployed, year, social category and State-wise, particularly district-wise for Uttar Pradesh;

(c) the funds including stipends sanctioned, released and utilised since 2021, year and Statewise, particularly for Uttar Pradesh;

16.12.2025 458

(d) the number of empanelled training institutions, quality-assessment mechanisms and measures to ensure industry-aligned courses and wage/self- employment linkages, State and district-wise, particularly for Uttar Pradesh; and (e) the reports of gaps such as training quality issues, weak placement linkages, stipend delays or lack of post-training support and the corrective steps taken in this regard?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS,

FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE

MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT (SHRI B. L.

VERMA):

(a) and (b) Pradhan Mantri Dakshata Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi Yojana (PM-DAKSH) Scheme is a Central Sector Scheme, introduced in 2020-21 to provide skill development training to SCs, OBCs, EWSs, DNTs, Safai Karamcharis including Waste Pickers through the empanelled training institutes.

Under PM-DAKSH Scheme, National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) implements training for SCs beneficiaries, National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) implements training for OBCs/EWSs/ DNTs beneficiaries and National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) implements training for Safai Karamcharis including Waste Pickers. The number of candidates trained, placed and number of training institutes under the Scheme State-wise in respect of NSFDC, NBCFDC and NSKFDC is given in the enclosed Statement-I, II and III respectively. The district wise details for Uttar Pradesh in respect of NSFDC, NBCFDC and NSKFDC is given in the enclosed Statement-16.12.2025 459 IV, V and VI respectively.

(c) As PM-DAKSH is a Central Sector Scheme, funds are not allocated and released State-wise. Under the Scheme, Department releases funds to the implementing agencies. The details of funds utilized State-wise by NSFDC, NBCFDC and NSKFDC is given in the enclosed Statement-VII, VIII and IX respectively.

(d) The number of empaneled training institutions State-wise in respect of NSFDC, NBCFDC and NSKFDC is given in the enclosed Statement-I, II and III respectively. The district wise number for Uttar Pradesh in respect of NSFDC, NBCFDC and NSKFDC is given in the enclosed Statement-IV, V and VI respectively.

Under the Scheme, the NSQF aligned courses were sanctioned, assessment of candidates is done by the third party agency empaneled by National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) to ensure quality training. As per norms, the training institutes are required to provide job/self-employment opportunities to at least 70% of trained candidates under Short Term Training Programme.

(e) Continuous monitoring of ongoing trainings are undertaken through online/physical mode. On identification of any gaps, training institutes are intimated for immediate corrective actions. With respect to placement, 3rd installment of course fee in case of Short Term Training Programme is linked with placement. Further, on non adherence of the target, the said payments are withheld and training institute is intimated accordingly.

IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SVAMITVA IN HIMACHAL PRADESH

2623. SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR:

Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state:

(a) the district wise number of villages/hamlets surveyed under the SVAMITVA Scheme, the total area mapped, and the number of property cards issued to date and the Gram Panchayats covered, along with progress of drone surveys, parcel mapping, property card issuance and integration of ownership records with the State land-record system, district-wise in Himachal Pradesh;

(b) whether various State Government departments, such as Revenue, Rural Development, Survey and Settlement, and IT are coordinating effectively with the Centre for seamless implementation of SVAMITVA scheme;

(c) the measurable benefits in the State such as increased local revenue mobilisation, bank credit facilitated and land-dispute resolution after surveys;

(d) whether the Government has addressed technical challenges in hilly/forest areas through special guidelines, if so, the details thereof;

(e) the status of convergence with State e-governance platforms and national land-record databases; and

(f) the capacity-building and grievance-redressal measures undertaken?

16.12.2025 472

THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ; AND MINISTER OF FISHERIES,

ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING (SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS

LALAN SINGH):

(a) In Himachal Pradesh, under SVAMITVA Scheme, drone survey has been completed in 13,920 villages with an estimated area of nearly 55 sq km, where 5,419 property cards have been prepared for 364 villages. Nearly 38 lakh property parcels have been digitized. In all, 3,353 Gram Panchayats have been covered with drone survey and property cards have been distributed in 114 Gram Panchayats. All the property cards are digitally linked to State revenue records.

District wise details are given in the enclosed Statement.

(b) The Survey of India and various State Government Departments such as Revenue, Panchayati Raj, and the IT department are coordinating for seamless implementation of SVAMITVA Scheme in Himachal Pradesh.

(c) As per information available with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, there has been no reported increase in local revenue mobilization, bank credit or resolution of land disputes in Himachal Pradesh.

(d) There are no special guidelines issued specifically for hilly or forest areas under the SVAMITVA Scheme. The existing scheme framework applies uniformly across all regions, including hilly and forested areas. Wherever required, State Government and Survey of India adopt operational adjustments such as optimizing flight paths, using appropriate ground control points and conducting additional field verification to address local terrain-related challenges.

(e) As per information available with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, SVAMITVA data is not integrated with any State e-governance platforms or national land16.12.2025 473 records database.

(f) Survey of India undertakes capacity-building activities from time to time for officials including Tehsildars, Patwaris and other field staff, to support ground verification of maps generated under the Scheme. For grievance redressal related to property cards, the Himachal Pradesh Abadi Deh (Record of Right) Act, 2021 provides a 60-day period during which property owners may submit claims or objections regarding the draft property cards before their finalization.

2624. SUSHRI S. JOTHIMANI:

Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:

(a) whether the Government has mapped the current and projected demand for lithium-ion batteries in the country across electric mobility, consumer electronics and grid-storage sectors;

(b) the status of domestic lithium-ion cell manufacturing capacity, including operational Giga factories and those under construction;

(c) whether the Government has taken steps to secure critical mineral supply chains, particularly lithium, through overseas mineral agreements and domestic exploration;

(d) the measures in place to ensure safe disposal and recycling of end-of-life lithium-ion batteries and the progress made under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022; and

(e) whether the Government proposes any incentives in 2025-26 to promote indigenous cell chemistry innovation and reduce dependence on imports?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES; AND

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF STEEL (SHRI BHUPATHI RAJU

SRINIVASA VARMA):

(a) As per the NITI Aayog report "Advanced Chemistry Cell Battery Reuse16.12.2025 475 and Recycling in India" published in May 2022, the projected annual demand for lithium-ion batteries for 2025 is 40 GWh and is expected to reach about 210 GWh by 2030.

(b) The Ministry of Heavy Industries is administering the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme namely "National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage," approved in May 2021 with a total outlay of ₹18,100 crore to establish 50 GWh of domestic Advanced Chemistry Cell manufacturing capacity.

Under the PLI ACC Scheme, the Government is supporting the establishment of 50 GWh ACC capacity. Besides the PLI ACC scheme applicants, at least 10 manufacturers have announced a cumulative capacity of about 178 GWh in the country over the next five years.

Under the PLI ACC Scheme, the beneficiary-wise details of their projected and current cell manufacturing capacities are as under:

Sl. No. Beneficiary firms under PLI ACC Scheme Projected Manufacturing Capacity (in GWh) Current Manufacturing Capacity (in GWh)
1. ACC Energy Storage Pvt. Ltd. 5 0
2. Ola Cell Technologies Pvt. Ltd. 20 1
3. Reliance New Energy Battery Storage Ltd. 5 0
4. Reliance New Energy Battery Ltd. 10 0
TOTAL 40 1

(c) As per the information received from M/o Mines, M/o Mines has taken several steps to secure critical mineral supply chains, including Lithium, through16.12.2025 476 domestic exploration and overseas mineral agreements, which inter alia include:

i. The Union Cabinet approved the establishment of National Critical Minerals Mission (NCMM) on 29th January 2025, with a financial outlay of ₹16,300 crore from FY 2024–25 to 2030–31. The NCMM aims to secure India's critical mineral supply chain and to strengthen all stages of the value chain, including mineral exploration, mining, beneficiation, processing, and recovery from end-of-life products.

ii. Geological Survey of India (GSI) intensified exploration of critical and strategic minerals. GSI took up 195 critical mineral exploration projects in 2024–25, and 230 projects in 2025–26 across the country. Additionally, National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust (NMEDT) has sanctioned 62 projects for exploration of critical minerals during 2024-25 and 36 projects during 2025-26.

iii. M/o Mines has successfully auctioned 34 blocks of critical minerals.

iv. M/o Mines has successfully auctioned 7 blocks of Exploration License, out of which, three are of critical minerals.

v. Khanij Bidesh India Limited (KABIL) is a Joint Venture Company under the aegis of the M/o Mines, has acquired five lithium brine blocks in the Catamarca province of Argentina for exploration and development.

vi. M/o Mines engages in various multilateral and bilateral platforms such as Minerals Security Partnership (MSP), India-US Strategic Mineral Recovery Initiative, Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF), and India-UK Technology Security Initiative (TSI), etc. for strengthening the critical16.12.2025 477 minerals value chain.

(d) As per information provided by M/o Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), the MoEFCC has notified Battery Waste Management Rules (BWMR), 2022, dated 24th August 2022, to ensure environmentally sound management of waste batteries. The rules cover all types of batteries, including Lithium-Ion batteries. Under the rules, the producers, including importers, have been given mandatory Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) targets for collection and recycling or refurbishment of waste batteries.

A Centralized online EPR portal has been developed for registration of producers and recyclers/ refurbishers, to facilitate the exchange of EPR certificates between producers and recyclers/ refurbishers and filing returns by producers and recyclers/ refurbishers. So far, 3,391 producers of lithium-ion batteries and 43 recyclers of lithium-ion batteries have registered on the portal.

Around 15,370 tonnes of lithium-ion battery waste has been recycled till date since the notification of the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022.

(e) The PLI ACC scheme is technologically agnostic, which ensures that superior technologies receive higher incentives. The scheme is designed to attract substantial investments, promote research and development, and reduce dependency on imports for ACCs. Further, under the scheme, expenditures incurred by beneficiary firms on Research and Development are permitted to meet investment criteria, allowing them to integrate the latest technology in the implementation of their projects.

AMENDMENT OF BILL FOR MANUAL SCAVENGERS

2626. SHRI S. VENKATESAN:

Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:

(a) the reasons for dropping the bill for complete mechanisation of sewer cleaning through the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation (Amendment) Bill, 2020 ;

(b) whether any alternate efforts in place of the proposed Bill have been successful; and

(c) if so, the details of the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation (Amendment) Bill, 2020 is aiming at complete mechanization of cleaning sewers and septic tanks?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND

EMPOWERMENT (SHRI RAMDAS ATHAWALE):

(a) The Prohibition of Employment and Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation (Amendment) Bill 2020 envisaged for creation of Sanitation Authority; making State Government responsible for paying compensation in the16.12.2025 482 event of death due to hazardous cleaning activity and mechanization of hazardous cleaning operations.

Since, the above issues have been taken care of under National Action for Mechanized Sanitation Eco-system (NAMASTE) scheme and Swachchh Bharat Mission 2.0, the amendment Bill was not pursued.

(b) Department of Social Justice and Empowerment in convergence with Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs launched the "National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE)" Scheme in 2023-24 for its implementation in all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) of the country. The objective is to ensure safety and dignity of Safai Karmacharis and to empower them socially and economically. The aim is to achieve zero fatality in sanitation work and to ensure that no sanitation worker comes in direct contact with human faecal matter. The interventions under the NAMASTE scheme are as under:-

(i) Profiling and validation of Sewer and Septic Tank Workers (SSWs);

(ii) PPE kits for SSWs;

(iii) Occupational Training to SSWs;

(iv) Ayushman Bharat – PMJAY cards;

(v) Safety Devices to Emergency Response Sanitation Units;

(vi) Upfront Capital Subsidy to SSWs and Private Sanitation Service Operators for sanitation related machine /equipment;

(vii) Workshop on hazardous cleaning operations

Achievements under NAMASTE scheme are as under:-

• 89,104 Sewer and Septic Tank Workers (SSWs) have been validated.

16.12.2025 483

• 85,743 PPE kits for SSWs and 653 Safety Devices Kit for Emergency Response Sanitation Units have been dispatched to States/UTs.

• 70,950 beneficiaries have been covered under Ayushman Bharat –PMJAY;

State Health Scheme and under NAMASTE scheme.

• Capital Subsidy of Rs. 23.91 Crore released to 782 sanitation workers and their dependents for sanitation related projects.

• 1188 workshops have been conducted on Prevention of Hazardous Cleaning of Sewer and Septic Tanks.

(c) Reply has been made in part (a) of the question.

HANDING OVER OF SALT LAND

2627. SHRI MATHESWARAN V. S.:

Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:

(a) whether the Salt Department which comes under Ministry of Commerce and Industry is not complying with order of Supreme Court in SLP (C) 4632 of 2021 dated 13.10.2025 where the court specifically directed to hand over the salt land to the successful bidder/ Intervenor;

(b) whether any representation have been received by Salt Commissioner, Jaipur and Deputy Salt Commissioner, Chennai to comply the order of Supreme Court in SLP (C) 4632 of 2021 dated 13.10.2025, if so, the details thereof including the details of action taken on the representation;

(c) whether the Government is aware of the fact that not a single salt is manufactured for past twenty years in Salt Circle, Odisha which causing16.12.2025 484 loss the Government, despite there being valid tender process held in accordance with law; and

(d) if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND

INDUSTRY; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF

ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI JITIN

PRASADA):

(a) and (b) A representation dated 24.10.2025 has been received by Salt Commissioner Organization whereby the order of Hon'ble Supreme Court dated 13.10.2025 in SLP (C) 4632 of 2021 has been referred and the Department has been requested for transfer of 946.736 acres of Salt land in Humma Salt circle, Odisha on lease basis. However, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has granted liberty to the Central Government to decide on the matter as per law. No specific direction has been issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for compliance by this Department.

(c) and (d) As per available data, around 2,94,765 MT salt has been produced in the last 20 years in Humma Salt Circle, Odisha.

RECORD KHARIF RICE OUTPUT

2630. THIRU DAYANIDHI MARAN:

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state:

(a) the first advance estimate for 2025-26 kharif-rice output and whether the Ministry has calculated the expected procurement requirement, buffer stock levels and expected additional burden on public warehousing and PDS pipeline;

(b) the manner in which the Ministry plans to ensure fair and timely procurement and MSP payments to small and marginal farmers across all States, especially in regions struggling with storage or transport bottlenecks;

(c) the measures being taken to prevent post-harvest losses, waste and spoilage given the sharp increase in rice output, including expansion of cold storage, warehousing and modern silos;

(d) whether there is a crop-diversification plan to address the observed decline in pulses and oilseeds output and to reduce dependence on rice monoculture;

and

(e) the manner in which the Government ensures sustainable water use and climate-resilience practices in rice cultivation given record output, possibly requiring increased irrigation or groundwater extraction?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND

FARMERS WELFARE (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR):

(a) First advance estimates for 2025-26 Kharif is for 12,45,03,940 MT of rice.

16.12.2025 491

The paddy procurement estimates (in terms of rice) fixed during KMS 2025-26 (Kharif crop) under Central Pool are given in the enclosed Statement.

(b) To ensure the benefit of MSP to farmers, central nodal agencies (CNAs) in coordination with State Government and State Level Agencies (SLAs) open adequate procurement centres for convenience of farmers. Wide publicity and awareness are conducted through print, electronic and social media to ensure that all registered farmers may take advantage of MSP procurement. Payment to pre-registered farmers under PSS is made directly into their bank accounts through Aadhaar authenticated Direct Benefits Transfer (DBT)/ Aadhar verified Bank Account mode only.

(c) Government through FCI mainly stores wheat and rice after procurement for PDS operation and to maintain buffer stock. As on 01.11.2025, total Covered Storage Capacity available with FCI is 482.23 LMT (Owned – 147.38 LMT + Hired – 322.43 LMT+ CAP-12.42 LMT) and 347.13 LMT covered capacity available with the State agencies for storage of Central Pool foodgrain stock across the country. Besides, 432.93 LMT storage capacity is with state agencies.

Continous assessment and monitoring of the storage capacity is done and based on the storage gap assessment, the storage capacities are created/hired through following schemes:

1. Private Entrepreneurs Guarantee (PEG) Scheme

2. Central Sector Scheme (CSS) 2017-25

3. Construction of Silo's under PPP mode

4. Hiring of godown from CWCs/SWCs/State Agencies16.12.2025 492 5. Hiring of godown through Private Warehousing Scheme (PWS).

6. Creation of godowns under Asset Monetization

7. CAP Hiring Scheme -2025

8. Modified PEG scheme for NE and Hilly states with longer guarantee period of 15 years.

Creation of modern steel silos:

Food Corporation of India (FCI's) operational steel-silo capacity has increased to 29.5 LMT, with projects underway to raise it to nearly 90 LMT in coming 2-3 years, marking a major shift from traditional godown-based storage to modern scientific systems.

Main objective of this reform is to modernize India's food grain storage and supply chain through durable, efficient and technologically advanced steel silos that reduce post-harvest losses, preserve grain quality, enable faster and safer rail-based movement, requires one third of the land in comparison to conventional godown, and lower logistics costs.

Silos ensure better grain quality, reduced wastage and improving. For the sector, silos provide higher operational efficiency, faster bulk handling, reduced spoilage, lower labour needs and optimized supply-chain operations, strengthening the long-term storage capacity and enhancing sustainability and cost-effectiveness.

The total number of Operational cold storages of Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) state-wise are as under:-

16.12.2025 493
S.No. State Location Capacity in MT
1. Maharashtra CW Vashi 395
2. Maharashtra CW Nasik 2300
3. Gujarat CW Vadodara 1250

(d) Government of India is implementing the Crop Diversification Programme (CDP) under Pradhan Mantri - Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) scheme in the Original Green Revolution States Haryana, Punjab and Western Uttar Pradesh since 2013-14 to divert the area of water intensive paddy crop to alternative crops, which require less water under CDP, assistance is given for alternative crop demonstrations, farm mechanization and value addition, site specific activities and contingency for awareness and capacity building. Further, Crop Diversification Programme has been extended to major tobacco growing states to encourage tobacco growing farmers to shift to alternate crops/cropping system w.e.f. 2015-16.

(e) Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is implementing National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) project that studies the impact of climate change on agriculture. Under the project, risk and vulnerability assessment to climate change has been carried out for 651 agricultural districts as per Inter-governmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) protocols. 310 districts were identified as vulnerable out of which 109 districts have been categorized as 'very high' and 201 districts as 'highly' vulnerable. For enhancing the resilience and adaptive capacity of farmers to climate variability, location- specific climate resilient technologies such as system of rice intensification,16.12.2025 494 aerobic rice, direct seeding of rice, zero till wheat sowing etc. have been demonstrated under the project through KVKs in 151 districts covering 448 Climate Resilient Villages. Drought and flood tolerant climate-resilient varieties of rice, were demonstrated in several NICRA villages. Besides, training programmes are conducted under Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA) on various issues of agricultural practices.

Under NICRA, technical assistance for small and marginal farmers is extended to additional vulnerable districts beyond the 151 currently covered districts, to promote adoption of climate-resilient practices. Village level institutions through farmers' participatory approach, such as Village Climate Risk Management Committees, seed and fodder banks have been established for smooth functioning and need based technology penetration. The project is contributing to farmers' capacity building and improved crop yields, thereby leading to the socio-economic development.

Several schemes have been initiated under National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), to promote sustainable agriculture practices.

Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) scheme increases water use efficiency at the farm level through micro irrigation technologies i.e. drip and sprinkler. Rainfed Area Development focuses on Integrated Farming System for enhancing productivity and minimizing risks associated with climatic variability. The Soil Health and Fertility scheme promotes integrated nutrient management through judicious use of chemical fertilizers. Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture, Agroforestry and National Bamboo Mission also promote climate resilience in16.12.2025 495 agriculture. Further, Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana along with weather index based Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme provide a comprehensive insurance cover against crop failure by providing financial support to farmers suffering crop loss/damage arising out of unforeseen natural calamities. ICAR has released 2900 varieties during last 10 years (2014-2024) of which 2661 varieties are tolerant to one or more biotic and/or abiotic stresses.

PROPERTY CARD ISSUANCE UNDER SVAMITVA

2632. CAPTAIN BRIJESH CHOWTA:

Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to State:

(a) the manner in which the Ministry is working with banks and financial institutions to track and promote the use of property cards for securing16.12.2025 500 institutional credit for rural citizens;

(b) the current status of implementation of the SVAMITVA Scheme in Dakshina Kannada district of Karnataka, including the number of villages surveyed and property cards issued so far;

(c) the timeline set for completion of drone-based property surveys in all revenue villages of the district;

(d) whether the Ministry has identified any logistical or administrative challenges from the Karnataka State government, if so, the details thereof;

(e) the status of integrating SVAMITVA data with Panchayats' Own Source of Revenue systems for transparent property tax collection; and

(f) whether any villages in Dakshina Kannada remain excluded due to legal/technical//tenure issues, if so, the reasons for such exclusions and the corrective measures to cover them?

THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ; AND MINISTER OF FISHERIES,

ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING (SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS

LALAN SINGH):

(a) The Ministry of Panchayati Raj has had several meetings and is in constant communication with the Department of Financial Services (DFS), State Level Bankers Committee (SLBC), Reserve Bank of India (RBI), as well as Banks to track and promote the use of property cards for securing institutional credit for rural citizens. The State Level Bankers Committee (SLBC) usually has an agenda item pertaining to credit against SVAMITVA property cards to facilitate the acceptance of property cards for mortgage purpose.

16.12.2025 501

(b) In the Dakshina Kannada District of Karnataka the drone survey has been completed in 81 villages out of the total 422 villages and 2,605 Property Cards have been distributed in those 81 villages.

(c) The SVAMITVA Scheme will conclude in March 2026.

(d) The Ministry has witnessed slow progress of drone flying, ground verification and distribution of property cards as challenges in the State for the implementation of SVAMITVA Scheme.

(e) The State has not integrated the SVAMITVA data with the Panchayats' Own Source of Revenue system for transparent property tax collection.

(f) The State Government has informed that the remaining villages in Dakshina Kannada district have not been taken up under SVAMITVA Survey due to the reason that this district does not have the Gramathana or compact habitation clusters. The habitations have a highly scattered settlement pattern.

LOSSES TO PERISHABLE CROPS DUE TO INADEQUATE STORAGE

2633. SHRI ANUP SANJAY DHOTRE:

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state:

(a) the data of the quantity and value of perishable crops specifically onions, lemons and

bananas produced by farmers along with the losses of harvested crop due to inadequate storage facilities during the last three years;

(b) the information on the market rates received by farmers for the aforementioned16.12.2025 502 perishable crops during their respective harvesting months as well as the average market rate throughout the year;

(c) the overview of any schemes or special incentives available for constructing necessary special type storage facilities for these perishable crops such as onions, lemons and bananas, district-wise; and

(d) the details on any studies conducted regarding the potential for extending the shelf life of perishable crops including onions, lemons and bananas produced by farmers, a onetime investment and benefit to farmers at a large?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND

FARMERS WELFARE (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR):

(a) Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI), Government of India, commissioned a "Study to Determine Post-Harvest Losses of Agricultural Produce in India". The report, submitted in 2022 based on 2020-21 data, estimates that fruits and vegetables production was 255.56 MMT, with post-harvest losses of 19.33 MMT valued at ₹57,004.15 crore. For banana, citrus (including lemon), and onion, production and estimated physical and monetary losses for 2020-21 are as follows:

Produce Production in MMT Losses in MMT (2022 report of NABCON) Losses in Rs. Crores (2022 report of NABCON) Savings over 2015 report of CIPHET (Rs. in crore)
Banana 33.06 2.50 5777.01 145
Citrus including lemon 14.24 1.10 4347.13 1116.38
Onion 26.64 1.93 5156.32 667.62

Due to implementation of schemes in mission mode, adoption of improved16.12.2025 503 post-harvest technology, better storage infrastructure and enhanced training and awareness among farmers, post-harvest losses have been reduced significantly compared to earlier estimates.

(b) and (c) In India, harvesting and arrival of banana, lemon and onion continues throughout the year. Month-wise all-India weighted average modal prices, along with average prices received by farmers during the respective harvesting months, are given in the enclosed Statement.

Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is implementing several schemes under which financial assistance is provided for creation of storage and post-harvest infrastructure for agricultural produce, including perishable crops such as onions, lemons and bananas. These include Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) under ISAM - for establishment of marketing and storage infrastructure in APMCs, cooperatives and the private sector, Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) - for construction and modernization of cold storage facilities for horticultural produce and Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) under which concessional credit with interest subvention and credit guarantee is provided for creation of post-harvest facilities such as cold storages, ripening chambers and pack-houses.

In addition, Ministry of Food Processing Industries supports supply-chain and processing infrastructure through their Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana( PMKS), Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises Scheme (PMFME) and Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLIS-FPI) scheme.

16.12.2025 504

These interventions aim to minimize wastage, promote scientific storage and processing, enhance export potential and improve farmers' income.

(d) Scientific storage and control of temperature and humidity extend shelf life of perishable crops including onions, lemons and bananas. AIF and MIDH have supported such initiatives. Additionally, Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana- Remunerative Approaches for Agriculture and Allied Sector Rejuvenation (RKVY- RAFTAR) Start-up Program also supports innovations for better post harvest management.

TRAINING AND AWARENESS PROGRAMMES FOR DAIRY FARMERS

2635. SHRI MALVINDER SINGH KANG:

Will the Minister of FISHERIES, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING be pleased to state:

(a) the details of the planned training and awareness programmes for dairy16.12.2025 508 farmers in Punjab;

(b) the amount of funds allocated for these programmes and the amount utilised so far under these programmes; and

(c) the details of the frequency of the training sessions and the key topics covered therein such as balanced feeding, disease management and sustainable dairy farming practices?

THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ; AND MINISTER OF FISHERIES,

ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING (SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH ALIAS

LALAN SINGH):

(a) to (c) The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India is implementing the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) across the country including Punjab, under which financial assistance is provided for training to Dairy farmers, milk producers, and Dairy Cooperative Society (DCS) staff and members on good hygienic and manufacturing practices, clean milk production, milch animal rearing, adoption of balanced cattle feed, green fodder and mineral mixtures, and other related aspects. Under NPDD, for the state of Punjab, an amount of Rs. 445.63 lakh has been sanctioned/ approved and Rs. 109.75 Lakh has been utilized (upto 11.12.2025).

Under Rashtriya Gokul Mission funds are made available to States including Punjab for organization of fertility camps, milk yield competitions and calf rallies. An amount of Rs 58.97 crore has been released to the State of Punjab since inception of the scheme for activities and components approved under the scheme including funds for organization of fertility camps, milk yield competitions, calf rallies etc and Rs 56.4 crore. has been utilized.

16.12.2025 509

The training programmes are conducted in accordance with the approved training schedule and the participant coverage specified under the concerned scheme.

DISASTER PREPAREDNESS IN JAMUI

2636. SHRI ARUN BHARTI:

Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:

(a) the Central funds allocated for procuring flood and disaster response equipment for the Jamui district under the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF);

(b) the plan for establishing a permanent State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) unit in the eastern Bihar region to ensure quick response in districts like Jamui;

(c) the steps taken to train and equip the local Civil Defence Volunteers and Aapda Mitra in the vulnerable blocks of the Jamui constituency;

(d) the progress made in establishing a fully functional Fire Service Station in Jamui town to improve emergency response capabilities; and

(e) the measures to enhance public awareness on disaster preparedness through local Panchayats in Jamui?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI

NITYANAND RAI):

(a) As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the primary responsibility for disaster management, including disbursal of relief assistance on ground level, rests with the State Governments concerned.

The State Governments undertake relief measures in the wake of natural16.12.2025 510 calamities, from the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) already placed at their disposal, in accordance with Government of India approved items and norms. The Central Government supplements the efforts of the State Governments and provides requisite logistics and financial support. Additional financial assistance is provided from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as per laid down procedure, in case of disaster of 'severe nature', which includes an assessment based on the visit of an Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT). The financial assistance provided under SDRF and NDRF is by the way of relief and not for compensation for losses as suffered/ claimed. The details of funds allocated and released under SDRF and NDRF to all states including Bihar, is available on the website of the Ministry, https://ndmindia.mha.gov.in/ndmi/responsefund.

(b) Establishing a permanent State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) unit in the eastern Bihar region is the subject matter of the state.

(c) Jamui is not a notified Civil Defence (CD) District. Hence, no CD setup exists in the Jamui district.

In order to enhance the disaster preparedness and response capacity at the local level in the country, Upscaling of Aapda Mitra scheme, with an outlay of Rs. 369.40 Crore, had been implemented in the country in October 2021.

Under that scheme, Jamui was one of the districts covered with a target of training 300 volunteers.

With the learning and experience of the earlier scheme Upscaling of16.12.2025 511 Aapda Mitra Scheme (UAMS), the Central Government has initiated another scheme called Yuva Aapda Mitra Scheme(YAMS). Under this scheme, Jamui district has been also covered with a target to train 300 National Cadet Corps (NCC),150 National Service Scheme (NSS) ,150 Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS) and 30 from Bharat Scouts and Guides (BSandG) volunteers.

(d) As per the Constitution of India, Article 243 (W), Schedule XII, Entry No. 7, maintenance of Fire Service is a Municipal function in the States and it is primarily for the State Government to ensure safety of life and property from fire accidents and other emergencies. Directorate General Fire Service, Civil Defence and Home Guards, Ministry of Home Affairs plays an advisory role in the fire safety and service related matters. Further, Government of India has allocated Rs. 255.69 Cr. for the expansion and modernization of Fire Services in the State of Bihar under the 15th Finance Commission Grant-in-aid, out of that Rs. 76.70 has been released on 11th June, 2025 as 1st installment.

(e) Preparedness and public awareness programs for integration of disaster risk reduction into Gram Panchayat Development Plans was undertaken in the month of November, 2025 for the State of Bihar by National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM). Further, State level capacity building programmes are being conducted regularly by NIDM.

Nation-wide awareness campaigns on disaster preparedness are being undertaken by National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). NDMA is in the process of implementing the Mitigation Project on Lightning Safety (MPLS)16.12.2025 512 across 50 districts in 10 states, including Jamui, District of Bihar. Under the MPLS, four panchayats of Jamui viz. (a) Khaira (nimanvada), (b) Laxmipur (sukhasan), (c) Jamui sadar (harla) and (d) Giddaur (Ratanpur) are covered.

NDMA also conducted National Awareness Programmes under MPLS at the panchayat level in Jamui during August–September to enhance community preparedness on lightning hazard and reduce lightning-related risks. The awareness activities included school awareness sessions, community outreach through street plays, quizzes, LED-van campaigns, distribution of Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) materials in each panchayats including the four panchayats of Jamui District. The Students and Community were engaged as safety ambassadors and they were sensitized on do's and dont's, the use of Sachet and Damini apps and essential safety practices before, during and after lightning events

FUNCTIONING OF THE TIA PORTAL

2637. SHRI TEJASVI SURYA:

Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:

(a) whether the Trade Intelligence and Analytics (TIA) Portal provides transparent, accessible, and comprehensive trade data to stakeholders, along with the key features of the platform;

(b) whether the TIA Portal will particularly benefit MSMEs, startups and small exporters by giving them access to trade insights that were previously available only to large enterprises and the manner this platform will support better16.12.2025 513 utilisation of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs);

(c) whether the Government has phased out older systems such as the Niryat Portal, Tradestat Portal, and Monitoring Dashboard in favour of the more advanced TIA Portal with automated data collation, API integration, and seamless data extraction capabilities;

(d) Whether the development of the TIA Portal, initiated in March 2024, will support evidence based policymaking, trade diversification, and targeted sectoral interventions;

(e) if so, the details thereof; and

(f) the steps being taken to ensure that stakeholders' feedback is incorporated to continuously improve the platform?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND

INDUSTRY; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF

ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI JITIN

PRASADA):

(a) The Department of Commerce has launched the Trade Intelligence and Analytics (TIA) Portal as a strategic digital platform to empower India's export ecosystem. By consolidating diverse national and international trade databases into a seamless analytical framework, the portal delivers transparent, accessible, and comprehensive trade intelligence for all the stakeholders. This integration equips exporters, policymakers, and trade promotion bodies with the ability to monitor India's trade performance in real time, assess global flows, and identify new market opportunities. The public interface provides India-level trade insights, while advanced features—covering global data, competitor analysis,16.12.2025 514 and sectoral trends—are particularly strengthen analytical capabilities of policymakers and stakeholders including Department of Commerce, line ministries, Indian missions abroad, Export Promotion Councils (EPCs), and commodity boards.

Key features of TIA portal reinforcing India's export competitiveness include:

i. Unified Trade Intelligence Hub: A one-stop shop integrating global and bilateral trade data for exporters and policymakers.

ii. Automated Analytics: Streamlined workflows replacing manual processes, enabling deep insights into India's bilateral trade with 220+ nations.

iii. Advanced Monitoring Tools: Dashboards such as the Trade Watch Tower provide commodity, market, and regional analytics, supporting diversification and opportunity mapping.

iv. Enhanced Visualization: Over 270 interactive visualizations across 28 dashboards improve usability, replacing legacy systems with comprehensive capabilities.

v. Automated Reporting: API-driven collation and extraction simplify access, while monthly trade reports (300+ pages) and surge reports (30+ pages) are fully automated.

The TIA Portal is more than a data platform—it is a strategic enabler of India's export growth, fostering resilience, diversification, and competitiveness in global trade.

(b) The Trade Intelligence and Analytics (TIA) portal would empower MSMEs, startups, and small exporters to gain a comprehensive view of trade patterns16.12.2025 515 across the nation. The public interface of TIA portal offers seamless data extraction for customized analysis and provides insights into top commodities traded with specific countries, helping users identify market trends and emerging opportunities. TIA portal empowers smaller exporters to independently analyze markets, products, and trade trends without requiring specialized technical expertise.

(c) The existing capabilities of the Trade Monitoring Dashboard and Niryat Portal have been integrated into the TIA Portal, along with enhanced analytical capabilities and additional features.

(d) Each dashboard in TIA portal is designed to promote data-driven, evidence- based decision-making to enable decisions for trade diversification, export opportunities in target countries and regions. With all line ministries, departments, EPCs and all concerned stakeholders, TIA portal will support evidence based policy making.

(e) Key modules like the Trade Watch Tower and Champion Products dashboard help identify market opportunities and priority products, while commodity analytics enables in-depth competitor assessments for strategic planning.

Automated workflows generate comprehensive monthly trade reports. The core feature of integrating global and bilateral trade data in the TIA portal facilitates comparative analysis, policy evaluation, and market prioritization, strengthening India's trade intelligence ecosystem.

(f) A dedicated module in TIA public page (https://trade- analytics.commerce.gov.in/public/contactUs ) enables feedback from the public16.12.2025 516 in real time basis as well as a dedicated email id ('Trade Analytics' trade.analytics@commerce.gov.in ) is being used to track feedback, provide access to government officials among others.

MIS-APPROPRIATION OF RICE PROCUREMENT FROM NASHIK

2638. DR. BACHHAV SHOBHA DINESH:

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS be pleased to state:

(a) whether the Government has taken cognisance of the reports regarding mis-appropriation of rice procured from the Nashik district through procurement scheme;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) whether the Government has instituted an enquiry to review into the issue, if so, the details thereof including findings of the investigation and if not, the reasons therefor;

(d) whether the Government has initiated any punitive action against those responsible and if so, the details thereof; and

(e) the action taken by the Government to prevent reoccurrence of such incidents?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND

FARMERS WELFARE (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR):

(a) to (d) As per the information received from Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), the Tribal Development Corporation (a procuring agency in Maharashtra) has communicated that on 2 May 2025 some local newspaper16.12.2025 517 published that Government procured Paddy is being sold in black market of Gujarat.

The Maharashtra State Cooperative Tribal Development Corporation, constituted an inquiry committee on 2 May 2025. In view of certain suspicious matters that have emerged during the course of the inquiry, the Corporation has ordered the seizure and locking of the bank guarantee of the alleged miller.

Also the officials from The Tribal Development Corporation filed a complaint in Surgana Police station on 22 May 2025.

(e ) The Government of Maharashtra has instructed agencies to install GPS in paddy carrying vehicle and installation of CCTV camers in rice mills.

NATIONAL MISSION FOR SUSTAINABLE STEEL

2639. SHRI P. P. CHAUDHARY:

Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:

(a) the manner in which the 5,000 crore National Mission for Sustainable Steel is encouraging secondary steel players to adopt low-emission technologies and what reductions in CO₂ intensity have been achieved so far;

(b) the details of the early results which have emerged from the seven and the timeline for scaling hydrogen-based steel production commercially;

(c) the way in which the Ministry of steel is working with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) to ensure reliable and cost-effective Green Hydrogen and green power for steel sector decarbonisation; and

(d) the details of the technological or process innovations by Indian Steel16.12.2025 518 Manufacturers demonstrate readiness for EU CBAM compliance and enhanced export competitiveness?

THE MINISTER OF HEAVY INDUSTRIES; AND MINISTER OF STEEL (SHRI

H. D. KUMARASWAMY):

(a) 'National Mission for Sustainable Steel' has not been launched by Ministry of Steel.

(b) At present, four pilot projects for use of hydrogen in steel sector are operational with timeline of 24-45 months.

(c) Ministry of Steel is working with Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) for successful implementation of pilot projects in the following manners:-

(i) MNRE has issued scheme guidelines for implementation of pilot projects for use of Green Hydrogen in iron and steel sector under National Green Hydrogen Mission.

(ii) A Project Appraisal Committee (PAC) has been constituted with the representatives from Ministry of Steel, Mission Director, National Green Hydrogen Mission, academia and steel industry. PAC is empowered for evaluation of projects and monitoring the progress periodically.

Recommendation of PAC is submitted to MNRE for approval.

(iii) A Steering Committee under the co-chairmanship of Secretary (Steel) and Secretary (MNRE) is the apex authority for monitoring and implementation of scheme.

(d) Steel is a deregulated sector, and the role of the Government is that of a facilitator. Government regularly monitors the overall steel scenario including16.12.2025 519 exports, imports, prices etc.

PUCCA HOUSES UNDER PMAY-G

2640. SHRI JANARDAN SINGH SIGRIWAL:

Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:

(a) whether the Government has fixed any target/timeline to provide pucca houses to poor people under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G);

(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise including Bihar and if not, the reasons therefor;

(c) whether the Government has withdrawn/modified the allocation of the houses from various States under the PMAY-G;

(d) if so, the details thereof, State-wise; and

(e) the total number of Pucca houses made and allotted to the needy people under the said scheme during the last five years in the country, State-wise including Bihar?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT;

AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS (DR.

CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI):

(a) and (b) In order to achieve the objective of "Housing for All" in rural areas, the Ministry of Rural Development is implementing Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana- Gramin (PMAY-G) with effect from 1st April 2016 to provide assistance to eligible rural households with basic amenities to provide pucca houses with a cumulative target of 2.95 crore houses by March16.12.2025 520 2024. The Union Cabinet has approved the construction of 2 crore additional rural houses in next five years i.e. FY 2024-25 to 2028-29 to meet arising housing needs in rural areas in the country. As on 11.12.2025, a cumulative target of 4.15 crore houses have been allotted to States/UTs out of which 3.86 crore houses have been sanctioned and 2.92 crore houses have been completed. The scheme has been able to achieve its major milestones of allocation of 2.95 crore houses to the beneficiaries and the Ministry is committed to achieving the target of pucca houses by the prescribed deadline of 31st March, 2029.

The State/UT-wise details of targets, including Bihar, allocated by the Ministry, houses sanctioned by the States/UTs to eligible beneficiaries and houses completed as on 11.12.2025 under PMAY-G is given in the enclosed Statement-I.

(c) and (d) The targets under PMAY-G are allotted by the Ministry to the States/UTs on the basis of eligible beneficiaries available in the Permanent Wait List (PWL) based on SECC 2011 and Awaas+, 2018 list after deletion/removal of ineligible beneficiaries by the State/UT by following the due procedure.

Therefore, the reallocation of targets is necessitated to achieve the targets within set deadline. The reallocation of targets is a regular process and takes place only upon deletion of ineligible beneficiaries by the State /UT subject to an overall ceiling of target of Scheme. The reallocation of targets is carried out as PMAY-G focuses on providing the right benefits to the right beneficiaries in the right timeline. As of 11.12.2025, no re-allocation of targets has been done under16.12.2025 521 PMAY-G during FY 2024-25 and 2025-26. The State wise distribution of targets is given in the enclosed Statement-II.

(e)The total number of Pucca houses made and allotted to the needy people under the scheme during the last five years in the country, State-wise including Bihar is given in the enclosed Statement-III.
